title: Static visualizations
text:
We’re familiar with the grammar of graphics from our familiarity with ggplot2. These principles have also been applied to develop the semantics of several Javascript plotting libraries, including Vega-Lite and Observable Plot. Let’s see how the grammar is implemented.
We’ll start with some data from the US Energy Information Administration, looking at energy consumption over time of different energy sources.


Code
energy = transpose(energy_long).map(
    item => {
        item.year = d3.utcFormat("%Y")(new Date(item.year, 0,1));// convert to date 
        return item;
    }
)
Inputs.table(energy,{
    header: {
        year: "Year",
        type: "Source",
        quadrillion_btu : "Energy use (Quadrillion BTU)"
    }
})
















Let’s start with some familiar visualizations:


Code
ggplot(energy, aes(x = year, y = quadrillion_btu, color = type)) +
    geom_point() + geom_line()+
    scale_color_npg() +
    labs(x = "Year", y = "Energy (Quadrillion BTU)", color = "Source",
    title="Energy use by source, 1973-2022")










Observable PlotVega-LitePlotly (R)




Code
Plot.plot({
    title: "Energy use by source, 1973-2022",
    x: { label: "Year", type:'time'},
    y: { label: "Energy (Quadrillion BTU)"},
    color: {scheme: "Tableau10", legend: true, label: "Source", columns: 1,
        style: {float: "right"}
    },
    stroke: {scheme: "Tableau10", legend: true, label: "Source", columns: 5},
    style: {
        backgroundColor: "white",
        color: "#145da0",
        fontFamily: "Atkinson Hyperlegible",
        fontSize: "14px",
        padding: "16px"
    },
    marks: [
        Plot.dot(energy, 
            {x: 'year',
            y: "quadrillion_btu", 
            fill: "type",
            tip: true,
            }),
        Plot.line(energy, 
            {x: 'year',
            y: "quadrillion_btu", 
            stroke: "type"}),
        Plot.frame(), // add box around plot
    ]
})













Tip



Plot accepts many pre-specified color scales. See here. Legend specs can be found here






Code
{
    const points = vl.markPoint()
    .data(energy)
    .encode(
        vl.x().fieldT('year').axis({title: "Year"}),
        vl.y().fieldQ('quadrillion_btu').axis({title: "Energy use (Quadrillion BTU)"}),
        vl.color().fieldN('type').title("Source"),
        vl.tooltip(['year','type','quadrillion_btu'])
    ).width(400).height(400);
const lines = vl.markLine()
    .data(energy)
    .encode(
        vl.x().fieldT('year').axis({title: "Year"}),
        vl.y().fieldQ('quadrillion_btu').axis({title: "Energy use (Quadrillion BTU)"}),
        vl.color().fieldN('type')
    ).width(400).height(400);
return vl.layer(lines, points).title("Energy use by source, 1973-2022").render();
}











Code
plot_ly(energy, 
    x = ~year,
    y = ~quadrillion_btu,
    color = ~type,
    text = ~type,
    type = 'scatter',
    mode = 'lines+markers'
    ) |> 
    add_trace(
        hovertemplate = paste(
            "<b>Year:</b> %{x}",
            "<b>Energy use:</b> %{y:.2f}",
            "<b>Source:</b> %{text}",
            sep = "\n"
        )
    ) |> 
    layout(
        title = "Energy use by source, 1973-2022",
        xaxis=list(title='Year'),
        yaxis=list(title = "Energy (Quadrillion BTU)",
        font = list(
            family="Gravitas One",
            color = "#145da0"
        ),
        legend = list(
            title = list(text="Source"),
            font = list(
                family = "Gravitas One",
                size = 14,
                color = "#145da0")))
    )
